trainers.instruction: This is a map of Eastern Europe. Select the forest to learn more.

atoms.b: Located on the ((++border fence)) between Poland and Belarus, the Białowieża Forest is one of Europe’s largest ancient forests.
atoms.sound: Located on the border between Poland and Belarus, the beeyow-vyasia Forest is one of Europe’s largest ancient forests.

atoms.b: The forest is home to the largest herd of wild European ((++bison pigs)) in the world. In order to preserve the forest, large areas have been made into nature reserves.

trainers.instruction: Read the text and select the matching image.

atoms.a: Ukraine is famous for its black, mineral-rich soil that covers around two thirds of the country.
Widely known as the “breadbasket of Europe”, Ukraine is a top global exporter of wheat.
Ukraine is the world’s leading exporter of sunflower oil.
17% of Ukraine’s labour force work in the farming industry.

feedback.finish: In recent years, the war in Ukraine has had a big impact on it’s farming, which has disrupted its total exports and the livelihoods of millions.

instruction.text: Select the mountain range to learn more.

atoms.b: The Carpathian Mountains span across eight ((++countries towns)) in Central and Eastern Europe, stretching from the Czech Republic in the north to Romania in the south.
The highest point in the ((++Carpathian Caucasus)) Mountains is Gerlachovský Štít, located between Slovakia and Poland. It is around 2,655 metres above sea level.
atoms.sound: The highest point in the Carpathian Mountains is Gerlarkofskee Shteet, located between Slovakia and Poland. It is around 2,655 metres above sea level.

atoms.b: Many different plants and animals can be found in these ((++mountains volcanoes)), such as Europe’s largest populations of wolves, lynx and brown bears.

instruction.text: Drag the boat along the Danube.
Read the text and answer the questions.

atoms.text: The Danube is Europe’s second longest river. It passes through or borders 10 countries and flows through 4 capital cities: Vienna, Bratislava, Budapest and Belgrade.
The river is a busy waterway that plays a vital role in both tourism and trade. Multi-day river cruises attract many tourists, while millions of tonnes of cargo are transported along it each year.
In contrast, the river ends in Europe’s largest wetland: The Danube Delta. This protected nature reserve is a sanctuary for a variety of wildlife, such as the great white pelican.
